consensus_summary: Justice is an essential attribute of God and the corresponding moral demand on people for rightly ordered relationships, impartial judgment, covenant faithfulness, and active protection of the vulnerable, overlapping heavily with righteousness.
book_summary: Justice is righteousness applied to right a neighbor who has been wronged—the right Way to live—with English often rendering the same Hebrew righteousness term as justice in such contexts.
consensus_core_identification: God’s righteous character/ordering plus the human duty of equitable judgment and care that sets relationships right.
book_core_identification: Righteousness specifically applied to correcting a wrong done to a neighbor as the right way to live.
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the primary cases to interpersonal righting of a wronged neighbor, while consensus admits broader divine-throne, retributive, forensic-justification, and structural/social cases.
rationale: Both identify justice with the righteousness/right-ordering complex in relationships; the book keeps that central referent intact but materially narrows extension and precision to the neighbor-correction application, producing boundary disagreement without replacing the core or inventing an uncovered referent.
strongest_objection: Printed texts (Gen 18:19; Ps 89:14) link justice to God’s throne and general household obedience without explicitly equating it to righteousness applied only in righting a neighbor’s wrong.
